McLaren's New McL 820 Supercar To Offer HDK Version, Reportedly Weighs 1,550 Kilos
45 photos
Photo: McLaren
What McLaren calls McL 820 is a brand-new supercar due in the first half of 2027, potentially for the 2028 model year in the United States market. Per fresh information obtained by The Supercar Blog, this fellow is coming in two distinct versions, packs a heavily revised twin-turbo V6 derived from that of the poor-selling Artura, and weighs just around 1,550 kilograms (3,417 pounds).
Internally referred to as P34, the newcomer presumably succeeds the Artura rather than both the plug-in hybrid supercar and the internal combustion-only 7xx series. McLaren revealed the McL 820 moniker in October 2026, and in typical Macca fashion, the numerical side of the name indicates maximum horsepower.
Metric horsepower, that is, with 820 ps converting to 809 mechanical ones. That figure alone puts the McL 820 above the revised Artura and the punchiest member of the 7xx family, but alas, the rumored curb weight makes it heavier than the model it replaces. Weirder still, the Artura could remain in production until 2028.
The Supercar Blog also reports that McLaren will retain the Artura's twin-turbo V6, albeit with many revisions. One source described the McL 820's engine as nearly new, a selection of words that clearly indicates more than software calibration and less restrictive cats for the exhaust system.
Instead of a 60- or 90-degree layout, the M630 in the Artura is a wide-angle affair that prides itself on 120 degrees. Only the Prancing Horse of Maranello produces a similar engine as of this writing, and both automakers decided on spreading the banks outward this much to lower the center of gravity.
Photo: McLaren A wide-angle sixer like the M630 is great in terms of packaging as well, delivering structural advantages in the process. Better still, that 120-degree V allows opposing cylinders to share one crankpin on a stiff three-throw crankshaft, enabling an 8,500-redline. On its own, this engine develops close to 600 ponies and 431 pound-feet (585 Newton-meters) of twist.
Together with the high-voltage battery powering the axial-flux electric drive unit, make that 690 horsepower and 531 pound-feet (720 Newton-meters). Pretty serious maximum output figures, but alas, the Artura has always disappointed in other areas. Not only does it sound a bit uninspiring, but its styling is best described as clinical when compared to that of the 296.
Regarding the purported high-downforce package, McLaren produced four such kits in the past three decades or so. It all started with the three-seater F1 in the 1990s, followed by the MSO HDK flavor of the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren. Then came the 570S MSO High Downforce Kit, followed by the 750S Le Mans special edition from 2025.
Celebrating the 30th anniversary of the F1 GTR's 1995 overall victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Le Mans delivers 10 percent more downforce than a standard 750S. From the raised carbon-fiber active rear spoiler to the revised front bumper with a larger carbon-fiber splitter and the louvered under-wing panel, it's easy to understand how McLaren extracted more downforce from the incredibly capable 750S.
The cited publication hasn't detailed the McL 820 HDK at all, but we can easily imagine that McLaren will lean on the lessons learned from the 750S Le Mans for this upcoming high-downforce kit.
Via // The Supercar Blog

Rep. Virginia Foxx. Photo: USDA
An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, has lost her seat.
Update: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. After a recount, Chuck Hubbard has defeated Virginia Foxx by 330 votes, and will go on to represent NC-5 in Congress.
Christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.
Foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation , and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government . Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard , a former journalist and native of the district.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
10 year old suggests EVs, climate action
For the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek . Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).
Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get , but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from ).
Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher , and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).
Christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who said “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”
Congresswoman’s response sparks outrage from mother
But then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram , where it gained traction.
View this post on Instagram
Emily said Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”
I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.
Foxx’s response filled with climate/EV disinformation
Foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.
Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.
In the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal ) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones . Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”
Foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.
But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.
Foxx voted against EVs, for giveaways to wealthy
Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘new’ electric cars.”
But she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just new ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.
Foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites . Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China . Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans .
Those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive , which is to say it reduced the national debt ( by $238B ), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.
But most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.
And she mocks a 10 year old over the trillions in debt she voted for
In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.
But I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.
He will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024 , from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change . Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.
Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess shows where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.
Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and currently sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.
Update: Foxx may get her just deserts – she’s currently losing her seat by the narrowest of margins
When we first wrote this article in May, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024 .
But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.
After a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide , bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.
Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.
And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district, after winning by 330 votes in a recount.
The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats .
Generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.
So they engaged in Gerrymandering , a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.
Top comment by James
Liked by 75 people
Foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.
View all comments
But it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired . Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “ Dummymander “. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems)
After a nail-bitingly close election, Foxx requested a recount . The margin is extremely thin , just 0.12% of votes, but today Foxx called to concede , making it the last decided House race of the election, giving Democrats a 258-seat majority.
Foxx previously vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

Spacecraft Reaches Asteroid NASA Hit Hard in 2022 for the First-Ever Space Crash Site Investigation
45 photos
Photo: ESA
Back in September 2022, humanity managed to do something it had never done before: it slammed a speeding spacecraft into a distant asteroid on purpose, as it looked to prove that, if need be, we can change the trajectory of a celestial body that might head our way to end us. And now, another spacecraft has reached the target asteroid to perform what will be the first-ever crash site investigation performed in space.
The mission that impacted the piece of rock was run by American space agency NASA, and it was called the Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART). It called on a spacecraft weighing around 1,280 pounds (580 kg) to slam into an asteroid called Dimorphos at a speed of about 14,000 mph (22,530 kph).
The research conducted in the aftermath of the strike confirmed that the impact was successful. It generated a plume of debris across 6,200 miles (10,000 km) of space, and slowed the orbit the Dimorphos asteroid followed around its bigger sibling, Didymos, by 33 minutes, a much greater change than predicted.
The historic mission was so important that it immediately triggered another one. This time run by the European Space Agency (ESA), it is meant to get to the site of the impact and have a look at it in a bid to answer questions about what the impact did to the asteroid itself, the crater it left behind, if any, and, of course, determine the composition of the rock to see how that affected the results of the strike.
ESA's mission is called Hera, and it launched in late 2024. It comprises the main spacecraft and two CubeSats called Milani and Juventas, which will be used to study Dimorphos from an up-close-and-personal position.
Photo: ESA The collection of hardware arrived at its target asteroids at the beginning of the month, a few weeks sooner than initially anticipated, following a two-year journey and 122 million miles (196.5 million km) traveled.
Now in position just 18 miles (30 km) away from the binary system 65803 Didymos , the spacecraft is getting ready to do its thing. According to the Europeans, it has already begun the early characterization phase, which has it collecting key data on the two asteroids.
Hera's handlers here on Earth hope it will deliver the first clear images of what an asteroid so small (Dimorphos is just 495 feet, or 151 meters in diameter) looks like after an impact of this magnitude.
Come December, Hera will move closer to the two asteroids, and it will begin the detailed characterization phase, which should give it even more insight into what happened and how the relationship between the two bodies has changed.
Photo: ESA Presently, the spacecraft flies around the common center of gravity of the two bodies, with the speed of a quick insect, moving in nearly straight rather than circular lines around the asteroids. For the phase coming next week, it will adopt a more complex bowtie-shaped hyperbolic orbit.
Early next year, Europeans will command Hera to move even closer for what is described as a crash site investigation. For this task, it will use the instruments it already has on board, and it will also deploy the two CubeSats it carries. These are tasked with actually landing on the surface of the asteroid to collect data.
When it announced these details, ESA also revealed that Hera has already snapped images of the asteroids. For one reason or another, these have not been released yet, but we're promised that will happen as soon as Wednesday, November 25, when we are to expect to see the bigger Didymos asteroid in all its close-up glory.
The successful mission of the small-car-sized spacecraft should make it obvious to us whether we have the ability to change the trajectory of an asteroid that might one day impact our planet – a key step in planetary defense efforts against such threats.
Photo: ESA If the findings are as good as people expect, the kinetic impact method used by DART could become the main weapon against potential death from the sky. But even so, there are so many factors at play here that a touch of caution wouldn't hurt.
DART hit a pretty small target, and there are much bigger near-Earth asteroids to worry about. Such a mission launched in a time of need would probably require much bigger spacecraft hitting their target much faster.
Or, at least, as far out from Earth as possible so that a minor change in trajectory there would translate into a completely different path closer to home.
Exactly one year ago, ESA said there were around 40,000 near-Earth asteroids out there – at least, that's how many we know about. Of that, some 2,000 of them have a non-zero chance of impacting Earth sometime in the next hundred years, according to the agency. Very close to zero, true, but not actually zero...

Black-on-Black Temerario Comes From Lamborghini Palm Beach To Twist Your Bank Account
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | lambopalmbeach
Lamborghini offers plenty of personalization options for its new-age lineup consisting of plug-in hybrids only. These include the Urus SE Performante , the Revuelto (and Revuelto SV), and the Temerario, in case you forgot.
The list becomes even longer if you factor in the Raging Bull’s personalization division, Ad Personam, which pretty much renders a chunk of the tuning game useless. Sure, it may not offer wacky body kits, but the customization is definitely interesting, and if you are looking for various colors inside and out, then you can find most (or almost all) combinations in the official catalog.
At first glance, the Lamborghini Temerario pictured in the gallery may look like it came from a renowned tuner’s portfolio. But it hasn’t, as despite the stealthy look, it is bone stock. In fact, Lamborghini Palm Beach recently dropped these images on its social media, accompanied by a few words. And to be honest, we do not know whether this example is for sale, or if it is nothing more than a simple marketing tool, but it is so cool that it will probably make some consider sprucing up their lives with one of these.
Photo: Instagram | lambopalmbeach The supercar in question features a Nero Noctis exterior. Th glossy black paint was applied to all body panels, as well as the wheels, and the only contrasting element on the outside lies behind the alloys. We’re talking about the lime green brake calipers with Lamborghini branding. The interior is decorated with a few red touches, and it consists of black leather upholstery, as well as a few suede inserts, and it is definitely something to write home about.
Since this particular Lamborghini Temerario hasn’t been touched with the tuning stick, it still has 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW) available via the right pedal. That’s how much the three electric motors and the twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine produce in total. The PHEV setup allows the brand’s new “baby” supercar to reach 62 mph (100 kph) in 27 seconds, and a 213 mph (343 kph) top speed.
Now, if this supercar has made you crave a Lamborghini Temerario of your own, then you should know that it starts at roughly $380,000 for the 2027 model year, before destination, options, and dealer fees.
Lamborghini’s Temerario entered production in 2025 at the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory. It “lent” its PHEV setup and other nuts and bolts to the Audi Nuvolari, and it is the Huracan’s successor. Some have criticized it for looking a bit bland compared to its larger sibling, the Revuelto , but to be honest, we (or I, in this case) think that Lambo has definitely nailed the design, as this is one head-turning machine. But would you rather have one of these or a barely-driven Huracan instead? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lamborghini Palm Beach (@lambopalmbeach)

The Abyss Park Tiny Is an All-Black, Super Fancy Take on Mobile Living in Two
52 photos
Photo: LA Manufactured Homes LLC
Who says a tiny house or a mobile home has to be cramped or even uncomfortable, lacking proper features and the kind of functionality that would make it suitable for everyday use? Well, whoever sees that needs to have a look at any park tiny out there, and this one in particular.
This is the APS 520MS from U.S.-based manufacturer Champion Homes. It's a couple's mobile home imagined as the perfect lake-front destination for an extended vacation, the entire summer, or even full-time living where permitted.
Like most park tinies being made in the U.S., this one, too, can be customized to a large extent, from the finishes to the appliances, fabrics and colors, with the only invariable being the layout itself. You can see several options in the photos in the gallery, from a more colorful unit to one with modern touches throughout.
Yet the iteration of the APS 520M that still stands out, even two years after it emerged on the market, is the all-black variation dealers called The Abyss. It's dramatic, it has a strong personality, and it's designed to make an impression, but it also serves as a great example of different this floorplan is from all the others out there.
Photo: Champion Homes This park tiny may be imagined as a couple's home, but it's still big enough to fall in the category of Park RVs. That means that, while still mobile in every sense of the word, it's designed to stay put on location after initial delivery, which will have to take place with a special towing rig and special permits due to its dimensions.
It's 35 feet (10.6 meters) long overall and 15 feet (4.6 meters) wide, and offers 399 square feet (37 square meters) of living space, which, when employed for the comfort of just two occupants, feels comparatively huge.
In other words, when manufacturers aren't pressed to fit in accommodation for more people or more features for the higher number of occupants, 399 square feet is enough space to make a proper, sizable, and super fancy home. Like The Abyss here.
Photo: Champion Homes The other thing that makes this park tiny different from the others is the way in which it strives to create the feeling of open, flowing spaces while retaining the possibility of privacy. It does that by adding multiple entries into the same space, which works wonderfully with the extra-high ceilings to create the impression of much larger volumes.
The home sits on a quad axle custom trailer and features as highlight a wraparound porch designed as an outdoor entertainment area. That means it has ample space for a table and seats or whatever outdoor furniture you prefer, as well as a large fireplace with a wood wall that will accept a large-screen TV.
The porch also offers access inside through two different points. There's the main door in front of the house and then there's a side entryway into the bedroom – the only one inside. This being a couple's home, it's a one-bed, one-bad, no-loft floorplan, which means just about every feature you can think of is residential in size.
Photo: LA Manufactured Homes LLC The layout puts the living room at the front of the trailer, the kitchen in the middle section of the trailer, and the only bedroom and bathroom at the back, sharing the width of the trailer .
The living room is framed by large windows on three sides, so it's always basked in natural light. As shown in both video and photos, it's large enough to fit a sofa and maybe a few other pieces of furniture, and will flow directly into the kitchen space with no direct separation.
The kitchen is impressive for any type of mobile home. It's a two-block unit with residential, extra-large appliances (including a dishwasher, which is now a staple in this type of park tinies), plenty of cabinetry for storage, plenty of counter space, and – again – plenty of space to move around.
Photo: Champion Homes Finishes are up to each customer , from the color of the cabinets to the backsplashes and counters, but The Abyss lives up to its name with all-black everything: cabinetry, appliances, and tiling. Even the sink, a double-basin one, is black in this one, which might not be the most practical color but it sure is striking.
The bathroom is technically a pass-through one, in that you can access it both from the bedroom and the little hallway outside the kitchen space, where you have space for a stackable washer and dryer. It's also a full bathroom, with a walk-in shower with glass doors, a plumbed toilet, and a sink on a vanity that you can choose to have matched to the kitchen.
The bedroom is also accessible from several points – three to be more exact. You can enter it from the bathroom, from the same hallway with the washer-dryer, or from the porch. If the two people choosing this park tiny as their new home are into playing hide-and-seek, they won't be disappointed .
Photo: Champion Homes Also standard in this home is a full wardrobe behind barn doors and a dresser of drawers in the middle. Champion Homes doesn't say anything about the size of the bed that would go in there, but it should probably be a queen if you still want to have walkaround space.
The APS 520MS comes standard with two mini-splits for AC and heat, a water heater, and RV-style hookups for water, electricity, and sewage.
Photo: Champion Homes Pricing for each unit depends on the local retailer (Champion Homes doesn't offer any kind of figure for their homes) and the finishes you choose. Either way, you're likely looking at a $110,000+ purchase.

Yambi Is a Retired Ambulance That Got a Second Life as a Functional Tiny Home for Two
23 photos
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot
Turning an old vehicle into a mobile living space, especially with little to no prior construction experience, is no easy feat. It takes plenty of planning, hard work, and a good deal of creativity, but embarking on such a project can be a highly rewarding experience.
For Aaron and Sienna, a couple who love the nomadic lifestyle, transforming a decommissioned ambulance into a home on wheels was an opportunity to build something that reflected their personalities and met their needs to a T. Their compact mobile home, named Yambi, is based on a 2021 E450 retired ambulance with a wheeled coach box and is designed to accommodate both their work and travel needs.
In the realm of DIY conversions, panel vans are certainly the most popular foundation for camper conversions, but out-of-service emergency vehicles seem to attract a lot of attention, too. It’s not rare for people to use old ambulances as a platform for camper conversions, as these vehicles are typically quite affordable, boast a sturdy construction, and are designed for heavy use. Not to mention, both their exterior and interior offer ample built-in storage solutions that travelers really appreciate.
Aaron and Sienna got the ambulance on an auction site and worked tirelessly on it for about seven months to transform it into the comfortable, functional home on wheels that it is today.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot The idea of adopting a nomadic lifestyle in a self-built mobile home came about after the couple graduated from college in 2024 and began looking for a more fulfilling way of life. Both of them landed remote jobs, which gave them the freedom to work from anywhere, and a three-month road trip helped them realize how much they enjoyed life on the move.
They started the project with no prior experience on this type of build. They are both engineers, though, and Sienna does a lot of DIY projects , which proved useful in their endeavor. One of the biggest challenges for them was that they had set a deadline. They wanted to have the conversion ready for their wedding in June 2026.
They managed to complete it in time and even drove Yambi to their wedding. In a personal touch, they invited their guests to sign the rear doors, turning the inside of these doors into an unusual wedding guest book.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot They didn’t do too many changes to the exterior of the vehicle, but Yambi doesn’t look like an ambulance anymore. Aaron and Sienna repainted the entire body in a combination of white and blue, removed the front light bar and side emergency lights, and replaced the rear lights with some small windows, but kept the scene lights on the sides, which come in handy for illuminating the area around the vehicle at camp.
The vehicle also retains the original entrance door and all the exterior storage compartments. One of the larger ones at the front got transformed into an indoor-outdoor shower, while the others provide storage for all kinds of necessary equipment, including the batteries, propane bottles, electrical system components, a 50-gallon freshwater tank, tools, and even a Blackstone griddle.
On the roof, the couple installed a custom roof rack made from Unistrut, a modular metal framing and support system, and they used leftovers to build a rear ladder for easy access up there.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot The ambulance’s interior has been transformed into an open-plan living space that balances necessary amenities with a unique aesthetic. Using the available space cleverly and taking advantage of vertical space, the couple managed to integrate all the essentials without making the interior feel crowded.
A sliding pass-through door at the front provides access to the cab, while the main living area includes a functional kitchen, a comfortable sleeping area, a small wet bathroom, and even a dining area and a dedicated workspace.
The kitchen is equipped with plenty of base and overhead cabinets, a large sink, a microwave, a compact refrigerator, and a separate freezer tucked away beneath the rear bed. For cooking, the couple installed a two-burner induction cooktop that can also be taken outside when they prefer to prepare meals in the open air.
Photo: Tiny House Giant Journey/YouTube screenshot One of the smartest features that allowed them to fit so much in such a small space is the extendable rear bed. Designed with three sliding sections, it retracts during the day to free up space in the living area and extends into a queen-size bed at night. They are able to stand comfortably in bed, and the three small windows added at the rear bring in natural light.
In front of the bed, they built a compact booth that serves as a nice place to relax. It transforms into a dining area as well, with a table that slides out from underneath the bed.
For off-grid living, the couple equipped this unique conversion with a 540Ah battery bank and 800 watts of solar panels on the roof. An OutEquip Pro air conditioning unit and a MaxxAir fan make sure the interior never gets too hot.
In terms of costs, the entire conversion came to about $40,000. Aaron and Sienna paid $10,000 on the ambulance itself and the other $30,000 were invested in electrical components, materials, and everything needed to transform the vehicle inside and out.

Networking
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ uplink ports 25 26
We bought a cheap Centec-based ZX530S-24S2CQ switch that we are reviewing as a generic switch. This is a 26-port Ethernet switch with twenty-four SFP+ 10G and two QSFP28 100G ports that can also run at other speeds. We purchased our review unit on AliExpress for just under $575, and multiple vendors sell similar units usually in the $480-600 range. It might be cheap, but the question is whether it will be any good. We ask because it uses a Centec CTC7132 switch chip. Allegedly, this is a 6th-generation switch chip from the company, but we have not seen it in our lab before and we have not seen a thorough online test of it. It seems to be more focused on sales in its domestic Chinese market. So, of course, we had to buy one (and another switch with the same chip) to see how it performs. The exact seller no longer sells the switch, but several are available online with model names that match the switch PCB’s silkscreened model. If you are wondering whether we found something interesting, the answer is yes… yes we did.
As a quick note, the video was sponsored by Micro Center . You can also find the unit as a Sodola (here is an Amazon Affiliate ) and on AliExpress Affiliate Search .
Centec ZX530S-24S2CQ External Overview
The front face places the management interfaces at the left edge and the data-plane port field across the rest of the panel. This first view shows the complete layout, including the LED status legend that runs along the top of the chassis.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ front
From this angle, we can see how the port field is organized. The SFP+ cages dominate the faceplate, with the two larger uplink cages set apart at the right edge.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ front right angle
The left side of the panel holds the management cluster. This angled view shows the console and Ethernet ports alongside the USB-A connector that sits between them and the first SFP+ cage.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ front left angle
Two loose L-shaped rack brackets with empty mounting holes are supplied for standard 19-inch racks, resting on top of the chassis in our photographs rather than fastened to it. The left data-plane section here shows the paired SFP+ cages labeled for 10G or 1G operation.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ sfp bank left
The same bracket pair appears again from a closer angle. This view also makes clear that the port numbering starts at the left edge of the SFP+ bank, with ports arranged in vertical pairs across the panel.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ usb and sfp cages
The management cluster contains a stacked CON and ETH RJ45 pair, status LEDs for power, system, ID and Ethernet, and a USB-A port. The separate ETH jack provides out-of-band access independent of the data plane, while the CONSOLE port serves local serial configuration.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ management cluster
This macro view shows the USB Type-A port positioned between the management RJ45 pair and the SFP+ cage bank. The triangle icon above it marks the connector clearly on a panel that is otherwise dense with ports.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ usb port macro
The included AC power cord rests across the chassis in this front view. This gives a sense of scale for the 1U form factor alongside the management ports and the start of the SFP+ bank.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ front with power cord
A yellow looped wire with ring terminals sits along the top edge here, likely intended as a grounding strap. The panel labels for CONSOLE, ETH, USB and the speed indicators are all visible in this view.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ front with ground strap
The main data field contains twenty-four SFP+ cages arranged as paired positions and labeled for 10G or 1G operation. This close-up shows ports numbered 1 through 24 across the bank, with the pairing marks printed above each pair of cages.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ sfp bank full
This detail view covers the left section of the SFP+ bank, showing ports 1 through 8. The 10G/1G label on the left edge applies to this entire group of twenty-four cages.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ sfp ports 1 to 8
The middle section continues with ports 9 through 16 in the same paired arrangement. This consistent layout makes cable management straightforward since each vertical pair shares a common center line.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ sfp ports 9 to 16
This close-up shows ports 17 through 24 at the right end of the SFP+ bank, with the vertical 100G/40G text visible on the right edge marking where the larger cages begin.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ sfp ports 17 to 24
At the right edge, two vertical cages are marked for 25 and 26, labeled with a vertical 100G/40G legend. In the benchmark they were used as 100G links with RS-FEC. These larger form-factor ports provide uplink capacity distinct from the SFP+ bank.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ uplink ports 25 26
The indicator panel separates per-port Link/Act positions for all twenty-six ports from a separate Breakout group, with color legends distinguishing speed classes. That layout helps administrators identify which LEDs correspond to normal port activity versus the upper-speed cage indicators.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ led indicators
Moving to the rear of the chassis, we find four cooling fans and an IEC C14 power inlet labeled AC INPUT 100-240V. A threaded metal fitting sits beside the inlet next to a ground symbol, providing a bonding point for the chassis.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ rear panel
This angled view shows the same rear panel from the side, giving a better sense of how the four fan grilles occupy most of the back plane with the power inlet at one end.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ rear angle
From this higher angle, we can see the top edge of the chassis alongside the fans and power input. The rear panel carries four fan grilles, with no additional venting visible along the side face.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ rear high angle
This macro shot of the AC input socket shows internal markings including BOYTALL BT-14-1 text and an adjacent grounding screw. The C14 inlet accepts a standard IEC power cord, so no special cabling is required for installation.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ ac inlet macro
The side profile shows mounting holes on the front bracket area. These provide attachment points for the included rack ears.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ side profile
This side view reveals a red circular QC PASS sticker near the left edge, two vertical columns of small mounting holes on the right panel, and a gold-colored threaded connector protruding from the far left. The chassis is otherwise solid metal with no additional venting along this face.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ side qc sticker
A gray Ethernet patch cord rests on top of the front panel in this close-up. The clear RJ45 connectors are visible alongside the SFP+ cages labeled 10G/1G and the USB-A port, showing one way administrators would connect management or data links to this switch.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ ethernet patch cord
This second cable accessory has a D-sub style connector with thumbscrews at one end. That connector form is commonly used for console access on networking equipment, complementing the RJ45 CONSOLE port on the front panel.
Centec ZX530S 24S2CQ console cable
The external design is straightforward and functional for a low-cost 26-port switch. The front panel clearly separates the management cluster from the data-plane ports, with the two larger uplink cages set apart at the right edge. We appreciate that CentecOS labels the port speeds directly on the faceplate, which simplifies cable planning in a dense rack. The included accessories are minimal but adequate: two L-shaped rack brackets and both console and Ethernet cables for initial setup.
Next, let us get inside the switch.
